title: comparison operators

lines.explanation:
If statement allows you to execute certain code only under specific 
condition. Equal operator '==' checks if two numeric values are equal 
to each other.
In this case if value1 is equal to value2 the program 
prints "equal".
In our case value1 is not equal to value2, so nothing is printed 
here

Operator '!=' means not-equal. Here we print the resulting string only 
if value1 is not equal to value2. In our case value1 is not 
equal to value2, so "not equal" is printed

If value1 is greater than value2  we print "greater than". In our case 
value1 is not greater than value2, so nothing is printed here

lines.code: if(value1 >= value2) System.out.println("greater than or equal");
lines.explanation:
Operator '>=' allows to combine two conditions. If value1 is either 
equal to value2 or it is greater than value2 we print "greater 
than or equal".
In our case value1 is less than value2, so nothing is printed 
here

If value1 is less than value2  we print "less than". In our case value1 is 
less than value2, so "less than" is printed

lines.code: if(value1 <= value2) System.out.println("less than or equal");
lines.explanation:
Operator '<=' allows to combine two conditions. If value1 is either 
equal to value2 or it is less than value2 we print "less than or 
equal".
In our case value1 is less than value2, so the string 
is printed
